newsitem.title: INDIA: PRESS DIGEST - Indian newspapers - September 13.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Indian newspapers - September 13.

text.p: Following is a summary of major Indian business and political stories in leading newspapers prepared for Reuters by Business News and Information Services Pvt Ltd, New Delhi. Telephone: 11-3324842, 11-3761233; Fax: 91-11-3351006 Internet : biznis.news@forums.sprintrpg.sprint.com
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
BILL ON QUOTA FOR WOMEN INTRODUCED

A constitution Amendment Bill seeking to reserve 33 percent seats for women in the lower house of parliament and state legislatures is to face a vote. The lower house of parliament will vote today. Parliamentarians, cutting across party lines, welcomed the move but felt the bll fell short of being comprehensive. The
PREFERENCE TO JOB-ORIENTED FOREIGN INVESTMENT PROPOSALS

Industry Minister Murasoli Maran said export-oriented foreign direct investment (FDI) proposals would be given priority for clearance. The FDI proposals, with the potential to create large-scale employment, would be cleared as a priority. But the minister said caution would be exercised while granting approvals because the government was committed to attracting FDI in high priority and infrastructure sectors.
BOURSE REGULATOR NOT TO CLAMP BAN ON SHORT SALE OF SHARES

Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI) Chairman D.R. Metha said the bourse regulator would not impose a ban on the short sale of shares. He said such a ban might curtail market forces. But if the bourse regulator found the existence of a group of individuals, which had sold heavily with the deliberate intention to bring down the prices, SEBI would take action, Mehta added.
BANKS ASKED TO KEEP 25 PCT OF DEPOSIT GROWTH FOR GILTS

The Reserve Bank of India (RBI), the central bank, has asked public sector banks to reserve 25 percent of their incremental growth in deposits for investment in government debt. Bankers fear that the RBI may ask banks to subscribe to the 20 billion rupee six-year government bonds auction announced for Tuesday. This is because credit offtake is weak, they say. The central bank has said funds released as a result of the cut in the cash reserve ratio should be put into the statutary liquidity ratio. For weak banks, the RBI has curtailed credit and directed them to put their funds into risk-free government bonds.
NEW NORMS ON CORPORATE GOVERNANCE CODE SOON

The government may issue fresh guidelines on the code for corporate governance, Finance Minister P. Chidambaram said. The role of nominated directors on company boards may be redefined. He told parliament he had asked some financial institutions to work with the corporate sector to evolve these guidelines. Chidambaram stressed the need for a strict vigil on the corporate sector's conduct. He said various irregularities had been noticed in the corporate sector and urged nominated directors to be alert and check these irregularities.
